rows.Origin:
Bred by Alain Meilland (1940-....) (France, 2000). Bred by Michèle Meilland Richardier (France, before 2000).
Introduced in United States by Conard-Pyle (Star Roses) in 2003 as 'Cherry Parfait'.
Introduced in Australia by Treloar Roses in 2008 as 'Fire & Ice'.
rows.Bloom: Light yellow to white, vermilion edges. None to mild, sweet fragrance. 35 to 40 petals. Average diameter 4". Large, full (26-40 petals), cluster-flowered, in small clusters, cupped-to-flat bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season. Medium, pointed, ovoid buds.
rows.Habit:
Medium, armed with thorns / prickles, bushy, compact. Matte, medium green, dense foliage.

Height: 28" to 35" (70 to 90cm). Width: 31" (80cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b and warmer. Can be used for beds and borders, container rose, garden or landscape. Hardy. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .

Jubile du Prince de Monaco is sold in the USA as Cherry Parfait, where it is classified as a grandiflora because it is a considerably larger plant.

Cherry Parfait is sold in Europe under the name Jubile du Prince de Monaco, It is also given a different classification in Europe, where it is a considerably smaller plant.
